introH2: 🏝️ What kinds of budget stays are on Koh Samet, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Koh Samet is known for beachfront resorts that run into the thousands of baht a night, but the truth is there are far more stays in the few-hundred to low-thousand baht range tucked around the island than most people expect — and that's exactly what makes doing Koh Samet on a budget more fun than it sounds. Some are air-con hostel dorms where every bed has its own curtain and power outlet, a few minutes' walk to Sai Kaew Beach. Some are in-town guesthouses where you can get off the boat and wheel your bag straight to your room. Some are modern loft rooms at a lighter price than a resort. And some are family-run stays that let you bring your pets along to the sea. Plenty of people pay for a beachfront resort and only use the room to sleep, when they could put that money toward seafood and boat trips instead. This article rounds up 10 budget stays on Koh Samet that we've reviewed in depth — across the Sai Kaew Beach area, the town by the main pier, Ao Tubtim, and Ao Phe. Every one comes from reading real guest reviews, telling you both the upsides and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites, with direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Koh Samet has no general private-car traffic. Getting around the island relies mainly on songthaews (shared pickup trucks), rented motorbikes, and walking. From Bangkok it's a 2.5–3 hour drive to the Ban Phe pier; park on the Ban Phe side, then take a passenger ferry (about 30–40 min) or the faster speedboat over to the Na Dan main pier. The stay areas in this article: Sai Kaew Beach — the busiest main beach, lined with restaurants and beachfront bars · Town / Na Dan main pier — within walking distance once you step off the boat, no songthaew needed · Ao Tubtim–Silver Sand — a quiet, less-crowded beach paired with a party beach, requires a songthaew ride in · Ao Phe — a quiet lane in the gardens, a 5–10 minute walk to the beach. Don't forget to budget for the Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park entrance fee when you arrive on the island, and carry cash because most shops on the island take cash more readily than cards.

entries.type: Hostel 2★ · Air-con dorm with privacy curtains
entries.name: Stay Samed
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Near Sai Kaew Beach · 6 min walk to the beach · 8 min to Na Dan main pier
tags: 🔌 Private outlet and light on every bed
🏖️ 6 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach
entries.addr: 35/5 Moo 4, Phe Subdistrict, Koh Samet, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: Among the budget stays we've reviewed on Koh Samet, Stay Samed has the highest review score — about 9.1 from 67 reviews on Hostelworld and around 9.0 on Hotels.com. The short version: this is a small hostel for people who want a clean bed, a location within walking distance of everything, and a light price, rather than a sea view outside the room. What sets it apart from typical cheap dorms is the investment in privacy for each bed — every bed in the air-con dorm has a curtain that closes on all sides, a reading light, and its own power outlet, plus a towel and basic amenities, so you sleep in a shared room but still feel like you have your own space. If you want full privacy, there are private rooms with en-suite bathrooms too. Location is the number-one selling point, because it's about 500 meters from Sai Kaew Beach, roughly a 6 minute walk, and under 10 minutes' walk from the Na Dan main pier — step off the boat and you can wheel your bag straight to check-in, no need for a pricey songthaew ride into the deeper beaches. A highlight that gets more praise than you'd expect from a hostel is the in-house cafe serving fresh coffee and all-day breakfast — several reviews say the food being good is one reason they scored it highly. Cleanliness, security, and friendly staff are things reviews consistently praise too. Honest caveats from the reviews: it's not right on the beach and there's no sea view from the rooms, so you have to walk out a bit; some private rooms look older than the website photos and can have damp or a musty bathroom smell in the island's humid weather; some beds run firm; and the vibe is fairly quiet, not a party hostel. If you're after a sea view or luxury, this isn't it — but if you want the cleanest bed, a good location, and a light price on the island, Stay Samed is among the best value in this price range.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For solo travelers, a dorm bed with a privacy curtain and full amenities is often better value and newer than a budget private room. If you book a private room, message ahead for the latest room photos first, and use the luggage-storage service after check-out so you can keep exploring before your boat.

Every air-con dorm bed has a privacy curtain, light, and outlet, more complete than typical cheap dorms
6 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach and 8 min to the Na Dan main pier, walk over straight off the boat
In-house cafe with all-day breakfast that many reviews call surprisingly good for a hostel
cons: Not right on the beach, no sea view from the rooms, you have to walk out a bit
Some private rooms older than the photos, with damp bathrooms and firm beds in some rooms (from reviews)

entries.type: Guest House · Central Koh Samet town
entries.name: Samet 99
entries.badge: 🏠 In town · run by the foreign owner
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Koh Samet town · 5 min walk to the pier and Sai Kaew Beach
tags: 🛥️ 5 min walk to the pier and beach
entries.addr: 153/8 Silver Park Avenue, Phe Subdistrict, Koh Samet, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: Among the few-hundred to low-thousand baht stays on Koh Samet, Samet 99 is a guesthouse that stands out for its central in-town location and hands-on care. Set on Silver Park Avenue in Koh Samet town, it's about a 5 minute walk to both the Na Dan main pier and Sai Kaew Beach, the same in either direction — step off the boat and you can wheel your bag straight to your room, no songthaew ride into the deeper beaches needed. The area around it is full of convenience stores, made-to-order food shops, massage shops, and boat-ticket counters, so food, supplies, and trip planning are all within walking distance. What real reviews mention most is that the owner is a foreigner who speaks English and looks after guests personally — one foreign review put it plainly: "the owner is the warmest, loveliest English person," giving detailed advice on travel, boat schedules, and restaurants on the island. Rooms are private with en-suite bathrooms, with air-con that genuinely cools, a flat-screen TV, fridge, tea-and-coffee set, hair dryer, and Wi-Fi that many reviews praise as strong and stable. The overall score sits at about 4.2 out of 5 on Tripadvisor (from around 15 reviews). Honest caveats from the reviews: most rooms are fairly small — enough to sleep in but not spacious — and some standard rooms, especially the inner ones, have no window to the outside, which feels closed-in; the number of foreign TV channels is limited; it's not on the beach and there's no sea view from the rooms; and it's a small stay that still doesn't have many online reviews. If you want natural light, ask for a room with a window — but if you want a clean private room in town within walking distance of everything and with hands-on care, Samet 99 fits this lineup well.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask about room details before booking, especially whether the room has a window, since some inner rooms have none and feel closed-in. If you want natural light, request a room with a window or a higher, airier floor. And message the owner ahead about check-in time and luggage storage.
pros: Central location, about a 5 min walk to both the Na Dan main pier and Sai Kaew Beach
Clean private rooms, genuinely cold air-con, and strong, reliable Wi-Fi (from reviews)
Foreign owner looks after guests personally, friendly, gives good travel advice
Good value compared with beachfront stays on the island
cons: Rooms fairly small, enough to sleep in but not spacious
Some standard rooms have no window to the outside, feels closed-in
Not on the beach, no sea view from the rooms · still not many online reviews

entries.name: Samed Yours House

entries.addr: 153/114-115 Moo 4, Phe Subdistrict, Koh Samet, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: Samed Yours House (some platforms spell it Samed Your House) is a guesthouse that fills the gap between hostel dorms and pricier resorts on Koh Samet — private rooms in a modern loft style at a low-thousand baht price. What earns it an overall 8.3 from 56 reviews on Trip.com is its location, which scores as high as 9.0, because it sits about 300 meters from Sai Kaew Beach, roughly a 3–5 minute walk, and a few minutes' walk from the Na Dan main pier — step off the boat and you can wheel your bag straight to your room. Around it are restaurants, beachfront bars, massage shops, and convenience stores like 7-Eleven all in a row; one foreign review used the phrase "just a 2 minute walk to Sai Kaew Beach," and many say the location is "very convenient yet still quiet enough." The room highlight is the loft style mixing exposed concrete with wood — the Loft Room and Loft Modern Room come with a big king-size bed, a large TV, and some have a balcony. Many reviews praise the rooms as cleaner and better decorated than expected, the big bed comfortable, the bathroom with good water pressure, and even small touches like the beach tote bag and umbrella the stay provides. Honest caveats to know before booking: many room types are windowless and feel stuffy and dark, which some platform descriptions don't make clear; some guests found damp and a musty bathroom smell typical of the island; soundproofing between rooms isn't great; and notably, there has been a review where a booked room was given to another guest. The advice is to confirm your booking ahead and pick a room with a window or balcony. If you want a well-designed private room in a good location at a lighter price than a resort, Samed Yours House is good value in this lineup.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Message the stay to confirm your booking right after booking, since there's a review that ran into a double-booked room. And if you're sensitive to stuffy or dark rooms, specify a room with a window or balcony (such as Loft Modern) at the time of booking, and ask to see the latest room photos.

King-bed loft rooms clean and better decorated than expected (from reviews)
Owner and staff friendly, quick to reply · beach tote bag and umbrella provided

cons: Many room types have no window, feel stuffy and dark; soundproofing between rooms isn't great
Some rooms have damp or a musty bathroom smell typical of the island

entries.name: Runa Runa The Best Guesthouse
entries.revCount: Booking about 8.0 · couples about 8.2 · Agoda about 7.8
entries.badge: 💸 Lowest starting price in the lineup
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Samet village · 5 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach · 700 m to Na Dan main pier
tags: 🏖️ 5 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach
entries.addr: 12/49 Moo 4, Phe Subdistrict, Koh Samet, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: Measured by starting price, Runa Runa The Best Guesthouse is the easiest on the wallet in this lineup — a fan room for two starts at about 600 baht. It's a small guesthouse in Samet village on the Sai Kaew Beach side, selling location and value above all. From the real reviews, the people it suits are budget-conscious couples, solo travelers, and groups of friends who want to stay overnight on the island more than they want a beachfront resort — and couples rate it especially highly, around 8.2 on Booking. Location is its top strength, because it's about 300 meters from Sai Kaew Beach, roughly a 5 minute walk, and about 700 meters from the Na Dan main pier, around a 10 minute walk — step off the boat and you can walk to the stay if your bag isn't too heavy. What many people don't realize is that Runa Runa isn't a single building but a cluster of several buildings with rooms at different levels, from budget fan rooms to air-con and family rooms; most have en-suite bathrooms, which are hard to find in budget stays on the island. Reviews consistently praise the rooms as clean, airy, bright, and quiet enough to sleep well, with restaurants, a food court, and 7-Eleven all within walking distance. For a guesthouse on the island it offers more than you'd expect — there's a 24-hour reception desk, luggage storage, currency exchange, laundry, a bar, a garden, a BBQ corner, and a counter for booking diving tours. Honest caveats from the reviews: the rooms and decor are simple and basic for the price; there have been minor reports of ants in the rooms at times; it's a stay in the village, not on the beach, so you have to walk out; there's no pool; some paths through the village are dirt and gravel, easier with a backpack than a wheeled bag; and there still aren't many reviews. If you set your expectations on cleanliness, location, and price, Runa Runa offers value that's not easy to match at the same price on the island.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Specify clearly whether you want an air-con or fan room at booking, since summer on the island is genuinely hot, and because there are several buildings, ask which building your room is in if quiet matters to you. Don't forget to budget for the park entrance fee when you arrive on the island, and use the luggage-storage service on check-out day so you can keep swimming.

5 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach and not far from the Na Dan main pier
Rooms clean, airy, bright, quiet to sleep in, most with en-suite bathrooms
24-hr desk, luggage storage, currency exchange, laundry, bar, garden, BBQ, tour booking
cons: A stay in the village, not on the beach, you have to walk out to the sea · no pool

entries.type: Guest House · Near Ao Tubtim–Silver Sand
entries.name: Samet Inn
entries.badge: 🏖️ Quiet beach paired with a party beach
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Tubtim · next to Silver Sand · songthaew from Na Dan main pier
tags: 🎉 Next to Silver Sand, lively at night
entries.addr: Ao Tubtim, Phe Subdistrict, Koh Samet, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: Samet Inn is a light-budget guesthouse that stands out for its location in the pretty-beach zone on the east side of Koh Samet. What makes it interesting is that it's near Ao Tubtim, a small, quiet, less-crowded beach many call the most relaxing on the island, and right next to Silver Sand, which has beachfront bars, music, and a fire show at night — so you get two worlds in one spot: by day you walk over to lounge on the quiet beach, and come evening you walk to the beach next door to socialize without taking a ride. It suits people who want a chilled-out beach day and a low-key party at night within walking distance. Rooms are private with twin or queen beds, and every room has air-conditioning, a flat-screen TV, fridge, and free Wi-Fi, plus parking. One review sums it up well: "facilities are limited, but it's fine if you just need somewhere to shower and sleep," which is the most accurate way to set expectations, because the group it suits is people who spend their time out of the room and come back only to shower and sleep. The overall score is about 3 out of 5 on Tripadvisor and around 7.6 on Booking. Honest caveats from the reviews: it's a light-budget stay where facilities are limited; rooms aren't large or new and quality may not be consistent across all of them; there's no pool; it's not on the beach and there's no sea view from the rooms; and you have to take a songthaew from the Na Dan main pier into the Ao Tubtim zone, since it's set further in from Sai Kaew Beach. If you measure value by a location in a pretty-beach zone that offers both quiet and buzz, plus a price lighter than a resort, Samet Inn does its job well in a budget way.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask to see photos of the actual room you'll get before booking, since rooms can differ. By day, go lounge on the quiet beach at Ao Tubtim; come evening, walk to the music and fire show at Silver Sand right next door. And budget for the songthaew from the Na Dan main pier into the Ao Tubtim zone — sharing the ride with several people is better value.

Rooms have air-con, TV, fridge, and free Wi-Fi, enough for a basic stay
Lighter price than a beachfront resort · parking available
Suits people who spend time out of the room and come back only to sleep and shower
cons: Facilities are limited, no pool · rooms aren't large or new
You have to take a songthaew from the Na Dan main pier into the Ao Tubtim zone
Not on the beach, no sea view from the rooms · Tripadvisor score about 3/5

entries.name: Smile Samed House
entries.revCount: Agoda/Booking about 7.0 · 234 reviews (most in the lineup)
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Near Sai Kaew Beach ~600 m · 5 min walk to the beach
tags: 🏖️ ~5 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach
entries.addr: 35/3 Moo 4, Phe Subdistrict, Koh Samet, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: Smile Samed House is a small family-run guesthouse that suits people doing Koh Samet in an easy-going way — couples or small families who want to save on the room and put the money toward seafood and activities instead. What gets it talked about is that it has the most reviews in this lineup at around 234, reflecting how many guests have passed through; the overall score is mid-range at about 7.0 across platforms. Location is the top selling point — about 600 meters from Sai Kaew Beach, roughly a 5 minute walk, and within walking distance of the Na Dan main pier. One review mentions the owner even came to pick them up from the pier; step off the boat and you can wheel your bag in without taking a ride. There are both fan and air-con rooms, all with en-suite bathrooms with a shower, a TV, and a fridge, plus free Wi-Fi and coffee, a 24-hour reception desk, a tour counter, and bicycle rental. What brings people back to mention it is the owner's friendliness and kindness — one foreign review recounts that despite a language barrier, the owner used a translation app to communicate and tried to solve problems, making it feel like staying at a relative's place. Honest caveats from the reviews: the rooms are very simple and basic; some feel the price is high for the room's size and condition; some beds are uncomfortable and bathroom water pressure is weak; at times no one can be found at the desk; there's no room service; and there are occasional water or Wi-Fi outages that aren't fixed as quickly as you'd like, while the language barrier with foreign travelers when problems arise also comes up. If you take to a homey, friendly style and set expectations to match the price, Smile Samed House is a warm, light-priced bed in a good location.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask clearly whether the room you'll get is fan or air-con and request the latest room photos before booking, since condition and price differ. You can message the owner ahead about a pier pickup, and if you run into water or Wi-Fi problems, contact the owner directly.
pros: Most reviews in the lineup, around 234 · warm, friendly family owner
~5 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach and within walking distance of the Na Dan main pier
Rooms have en-suite bathrooms, TV, fridge, free Wi-Fi and coffee · fan rooms from ฿700
The area is fairly quiet, no loud bar attached to the stay
cons: Rooms simple and basic; some say the price is high for the condition · some beds uncomfortable, weak water pressure
At times no one at the desk, no room service · occasional water/Wi-Fi outages
Language barrier with foreign travelers when problems arise (from reviews)

entries.type: Boutique loft · Mid-island near the pier
entries.name: I-Talay Loft
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mid-island, near the Na Dan main pier · ~800 m walk to Sai Kaew Beach
tags: ⛴️ Near the Na Dan main pier, quick off the boat
💧 Fridge + free drinking water in room
entries.addr: 11/17-19 Moo 4, Phe Subdistrict, Koh Samet, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: If your trip is about taking the boat over to Koh Samet and wanting a room that's mid-island, within easy walking distance of the pier and the beach without hiring a ride deep inland, I-Talay Loft fits that need exactly — and it's the only 3-star stay in the lineup. It's a small boutique loft-style stay of about 5–7 rooms with modern decor, set mid-island near the Na Dan main pier, the main boat landing, so you don't have to take a songthaew far inland once you're off the boat, saving time and the fare; and it's about 800 meters' walk to Sai Kaew Beach. Around the stay there's a 7-Eleven, restaurants, and massage shops within walking distance. The decor is a clean modern/loft tone, and every room is air-conditioned with cable TV, a fridge with free drinking water, and an en-suite bathroom with hot water. The overall score ranges from about 7.3–8.3 depending on the platform, with most reviews praising the clean rooms, cold air-con, friendly staff who help with boats and sights, and the very convenient nearby 7-Eleven. Honest caveats from the reviews: rooms are fairly small with thin walls, so you sometimes hear neighbors or the corridor; some decor and fixtures are getting old with signs of wear; check-in is sometimes slow when everyone arrives at once after a boat docks; and information about a pool is inconsistent across platforms, so don't count on there being one. If you're a light sleeper, choose a larger room not next to the corridor — but if you want a well-located base mid-island at an affordable price, I-Talay Loft is good value in its own way.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Land at Na Dan main pier and you can reach it on foot or with a short ride, no need to hire a songthaew deep inland. If you're sensitive to noise, choose a larger room and ask about a position away from the corridor at booking. And ask the stay to confirm the pool and breakfast directly before booking, since platforms disagree.

About 800 meters' walk to Sai Kaew Beach · 7-Eleven nearby
Clean modern loft rooms, cold air-con, fridge and free drinking water
Friendly staff who help with boats and sights
cons: Rooms fairly small with thin walls, you hear neighbors at times
Some decor getting old · check-in sometimes slow when it's busy
Pool information is unclear, confirm before booking

entries.type: Beach Guesthouse 2★ · Right by Na Dan main pier
entries.name: I-Talay Zone Sea Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 7.2 · 14 reviews · lower on some platforms
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Right by the Na Dan main pier ~80 m · ~10 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach
tags: ⚓ Right by the Na Dan main pier ~80 m
🏖️ ~10 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach
entries.addr: 11/19 Moo 4, Phe Subdistrict, Koh Samet, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: Among budget stays on Koh Samet, measured by proximity to the pier, I-Talay Zone Sea Hotel is the one that sits especially close to the Na Dan main pier — only about 80 meters away, under a 2 minute walk. It's a small guesthouse of around 13–15 rooms for people who weight a location where you can walk straight over off the boat and an affordable price more than a luxurious room or a sea view outside the door. The advantage is that when the passenger ferry from Ban Phe docks at the Na Dan main pier, you can wheel your bag over to check in almost immediately, no songthaew needed, and it's about a 10 minute walk to Sai Kaew Beach. There are both air-con and fan rooms with twin beds, en-suite bathrooms, a fridge, TV, and free Wi-Fi. What many people mention positively is the beachfront BBQ service, where you can book a grill set with a beachside table (for an extra fee), and a counter to help book diving tours around the island. Service is a fairly consistent point of praise, in contrast to the room condition — staff are described as friendly and helpful. The overall score is about 7.2 on Trip.com and lower on some platforms. Honest caveats from the reviews: the stay has been open since 2006 and was renovated around 2012, so many rooms are old for their age; rooms are fairly cramped; beds aren't very comfortable; air-con in some rooms is noisy or doesn't get cold enough; some bathrooms need updating and the bathroom walls don't reach the ceiling, so privacy is limited; Wi-Fi signal is weak at times; being right by the pier means some noise from loading activity; and value is something people see differently, since some feel the price is high for the room quality. If you value a location right by the pier above all else and set room expectations to match the price, this place does its job in a straightforward way.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose an air-con room if your budget allows, since the island's air is hot and humid, and message ahead for the latest room photos to check the condition before booking. The desk is open about 08:00–19:00; if your boat arrives outside those hours, arrange a key handover with the stay, and if you want the beachfront BBQ, book ahead.

About a 10 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach · both air-con and fan rooms available
Staff friendly and helpful (from reviews)
Has a beachfront BBQ and a diving-tour booking counter
cons: Rooms old for the building's age (opened 2006), fairly cramped, beds not very comfortable
Some bathrooms need updating · Wi-Fi signal weak at times
Some feel the price is still high for the room quality

entries.type: Budget Guest House · In an Ao Phe lane
entries.name: The Lost Resort Koh Samet
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Phe–Ao Tubtim lane · 5–10 min walk to the beach (not beachfront)
tags: 💰 Air-con rooms from ฿800, among the cheapest
🌳 Quiet lane in a tropical garden
entries.addr: 23/2 Moo 4, Phe Subdistrict, Ao Phe, Koh Samet, Mueang Rayong District
entries.storyHtml: Let's be straight up front: The Lost Resort Koh Samet isn't a beachfront resort with a sea view, but a budget guesthouse tucked in a quiet lane on the Ao Phe–Ao Tubtim side of Koh Samet, run by a British owner. The selling point is a price among the cheapest on the island, with air-con rooms from about ฿800/night on weekdays. It suits budget travelers, backpackers, or couples/groups of friends who plan to swim and explore the island all day and just want a cheap room near the sea. The thing to understand most clearly is that it's in a lane, not on the beach — from the stay, walking to the nearest beach like Ao Phe or Ao Tubtim takes about 5–10 minutes, and some stretches are uphill. What you definitely get is a simple air-con room with a TV, fridge, hot water, and en-suite bathroom; some rooms have a small balcony overlooking the tropical garden around the stay. A point reviews praise more than expected is that the Wi-Fi is fast and stable, working well in the room, along with comfortable beds and quiet nights, plus a garden, terrace, massage service, bicycle rental, and parking. It scores 3.2 out of 5, ranked #13 of 24 hotels on Koh Samet on Tripadvisor — numbers that say plainly this is a budget stay, not a luxury one. Honest caveats from the reviews: cleanliness and changes of sheets and towels during the stay are inconsistent; there are lots of mosquitoes in the evening because it's in the middle of a garden, not on the beach; some buildings and fixtures are old, worn, and rusty; the not-actually-beachfront location means an uphill walk; and a pool isn't guaranteed, since sources disagree. If you set expectations to match the price, The Lost Resort is a usable cheap bed for doing Koh Samet on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Bring your own mosquito repellent and spray, since reviews consistently warn there are lots of mosquitoes in the evening. If a pool matters, ask the stay directly to confirm before booking, don't assume there is one. And if you're staying several nights, ask up front for periodic changes of linens and cleaning.

Wi-Fi fast and works well in the room · comfortable beds, cold air-con, quiet nights
A few minutes' walk to the beach · garden, massage, bicycle rental, parking
British owner, can communicate in English with foreign guests
cons: Cleanliness and changes of linens during the stay are inconsistent (from reviews)
Lots of mosquitoes in the evening as it's in a garden, not on the beach · some buildings old, worn, rusty
Not beachfront, an uphill walk · a pool isn't guaranteed

entries.storyHtml: Closing out the lineup is I-Talay Focus, a small 2-star guesthouse in the I-Talay group with just 5 rooms, for people coming to Koh Samet to sleep as close to the beach as possible on the lightest budget, rather than to spend all day at the stay. Set in the Sai Kaew Beach area, the island's main and busiest beach, it's about 0.4 kilometers, or 5–7 minutes' walk, to Sai Kaew Beach, with small coves like Ao Lukyon a short walk away. What gives it charm and is rare among stays on the island is the beachfront cafe in front of the stay, where you can sip coffee in the sea breeze, and importantly, it welcomes pets at no extra charge, giving people who want to bring their dogs and cats to the sea an easy option. Every room is air-conditioned with cable TV, a private bathroom with a shower, and free bathroom amenities; some rooms have a balcony that catches the morning sea breeze. A point reviews often praise is the friendly, helpful owner and team, who recommend restaurants, dive spots, and getting around the island. Prices start at about 700 baht, and the overall score on booking platforms is around the low 6s out of ten, mid-range for a budget stay. Honest caveats to know before booking: it's a small 2-star guesthouse, so rooms are compact with basic facilities, with no breakfast and no pool, limited room cleaning, and cash only, which you'll need to prepare ahead since ATMs on the island are limited; and with only 5 rooms it fills up fast on long holidays. If you set expectations that you're booking a budget guesthouse, not a resort, I-Talay Focus does the "good value and near the beach" job well in its own way.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Have cash ready before you reach the island, since the stay is cash only and ATMs on the island are limited. With just 5 rooms it fills up fast on long holidays, so book ahead and confirm your check-in time with the owner. If you're bringing pets, tell the owner ahead, and plan your own breakfast at the restaurants around the beach or the cafe in front of the stay.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting prices from the standard-room range and may change by date and season; we recommend checking real prices and comparing 3 sites before every booking. The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, not from staying ourselves. Koh Samet is within the Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park, so there's a park entrance fee on arrival, separate from your accommodation cost. Prices on the island are generally higher than on the Ban Phe side because everything has to be brought over by boat. Budget stays on the island are limited and fill up fast during high season (Nov–Apr) and long holidays, so book ahead. Carry cash, since many shops and stays on the island take cash more readily than cards, and ATMs on the island are limited. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travelers often ask about budget stays on Koh Samet

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best budget stay on Koh Samet?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style · For score and cleanliness, Stay Samed has the highest score in the lineup at 9.1, an air-con hostel dorm with a privacy curtain on every bed and an in-house cafe · For starting price, Runa Runa from ฿600 is the lightest · For a well-designed private room, Samed Yours House has loft rooms with a location scoring 9.0 · To be off the boat and in your room quickly, I-Talay Zone Sea is right by the pier, or I-Talay Loft is mid-island · And if you're bringing pets, I-Talay Focus

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget stays on Koh Samet cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at about ฿600–1,200 per night · The lightest are Runa Runa from ฿600 and I-Talay Focus / Smile Samed House from ฿700 · Mid-range are I-Talay Loft ฿760, The Lost Resort ฿800, and Stay Samed ฿900 · Those starting in the thousands are Samed Yours House, Samet Inn, and I-Talay Zone Sea (฿1,000) and Samet 99 (฿1,200) · Prices on the island are higher than on the Ban Phe side and rise during festive periods

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Koh Samet and to your stay?
faq.a: From Bangkok it's a 2.5–3 hour drive to the Ban Phe pier; park on the Ban Phe side and take a boat across to the island (private cars can't go on the island) · There's both a passenger ferry (about 30–40 min) that's cheaper, and a faster speedboat that costs more, over to the Na Dan main pier · Stays in the Sai Kaew Beach / town / pier zone (such as Stay Samed, Samet 99, I-Talay Zone Sea) are within walking distance of the pier, while the Ao Tubtim or Ao Phe zone (Samet Inn, The Lost Resort) requires a songthaew ride to the beach

faq.q: ❓ Which budget stays on Koh Samet are within walking distance of Sai Kaew Beach?
faq.a: Many in this lineup are within walking distance of Sai Kaew Beach · Stay Samed 6 min walk · Samet 99 and Runa Runa about 5 min walk · Samed Yours House about 300 meters (3–5 min) · Smile Samed House about 600 meters (5 min) · I-Talay Focus about 0.4 km · I-Talay Loft about 800 meters · while Samet Inn is in the Ao Tubtim zone and The Lost Resort is in an Ao Phe lane, requiring a walk/ride to the beach

faq.q: ❓ Which Koh Samet stays welcome pets · which are right by the pier?
faq.a: In this lineup, I-Talay Focus welcomes pets at no extra charge, which is rare on the island (tell the owner ahead) · The closest to the Na Dan main pier is I-Talay Zone Sea Hotel, only about 80 meters away, walk over in a few steps off the boat, and I-Talay Loft, mid-island near the pier, quick from boat to room without a songthaew ride deep inland

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a Koh Samet stay · what should you prepare?
faq.a: Most budget stays on the island are small (some only 5 rooms), so they fill up fast · During high season (Nov–Apr) and long holidays, book 2–4 weeks ahead or more and prices rise · What to prepare: cash, since many shops and stays take cash more readily than cards and ATMs on the island are limited · the park entrance fee on arrival · and check return boat schedules ahead, using the stay's luggage-storage service after check-out so you can keep swimming · Every platform usually offers Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in a price like that first and comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com to get the best price
